documents.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
documents.text: Retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG, retrieves relevant documents from a knowledge base and provides them as context to a language model. The model uses that retrieved context to produce a response grounded in source material.

documents.title: Hybrid Retrieval
documents.text: Hybrid retrieval combines dense vector search with sparse keyword search such as BM25. Reciprocal rank fusion can merge the two ranked lists by rewarding documents that appear near the top of either list.

documents.title: Faithfulness
documents.text: Faithfulness measures whether factual claims in a generated answer are supported by the retrieved context. An answer can be fluent and still be unfaithful if it adds facts that are absent from the context.

documents.title: Answer Relevancy
documents.text: Answer relevancy measures whether a response addresses the user's question. It focuses on relevance and completeness rather than whether every factual statement in the response is correct.

documents.title: Context Precision and Recall
documents.text: Context precision measures how much of the retrieved context is relevant to the question. Context recall measures how completely the retrieved context covers the information needed by the reference answer.

documents.title: Ragas
documents.text: Ragas is an evaluation framework for retrieval-augmented generation systems. It includes metrics for faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision, and context recall.

documents.title: DeepEval
documents.text: DeepEval is an evaluation framework for LLM applications. It organizes evaluation around test cases and provides metrics including faithfulness, answer relevancy, contextual precision, and contextual recall.

documents.title: Evaluation Datasets
documents.text: A useful RAG evaluation dataset contains representative questions, reference answers, and document relevance labels. Versioning the dataset makes score changes easier to compare as prompts, models, chunking, or retrieval settings change.

documents.title: Hallucination
documents.text: A hallucination is content generated by a model that is unsupported, fabricated, or factually incorrect. Retrieval can reduce hallucinations, but evaluation is still needed to detect unsupported claims.

documents.title: Chunking
documents.text: Chunking divides source documents into smaller passages for indexing and retrieval. Chunk size and overlap affect whether a retriever returns focused evidence or an incomplete fragment.
